title: Domination: teams, fog and victory
summary: Set up a Domination war your way: free for all or teams, with or without fog of war, won by wiping everyone out or by holding 75% of the system.
text:
The **DOMINATION** start panel sets up each war:

- **Players**: you and 1 to 3 computer players
- **Teams**: **Free for all**; **2 v 2** (four players: you and Crimson against Amber and Violet); or **You vs all**, where the computers are allies and you take them all on (a real challenge)
- **Computer**: Easy, Normal or Hard
- **Fog of war**: off, or on
- **Victory**: **Wipe them out** (the last side holding areas wins) or **Hold 75%** (the first side to hold 30 of the 40 areas wins, or the last one left)

**Allies** win together. They never fight each other, and you can't send an army into an ally's area. If you and an ally take an area together, the bigger army holds it and the other joins it. In a battle you fight yourself, an ally's army fights on your side. Your ally's areas have a dashed rim on the map, and the player list says who's on which team.

**Fog of war**: you see the numbers only in your side's areas, the areas next to them and the fights you're in. Everywhere else shows **?**: who holds each area is always known, but not what's there. To see further, take an area next to it. Your area card says when something is out of sight, and you're still told when an army sets off for one of your areas. The computers play under the same fog, guessing from what they last saw. A player who has fallen to their last 3 areas is revealed to everyone, so a war never ends in a hunt.

**The end**: who won and how, how long the war lasted, a chart of the areas each player held from start to finish (a dashed line marks the 75% mark), and each player's most areas held, areas taken and lost, and army built. **NEW WAR** goes back to the start panel.

Starts are balanced for each setup: the smaller start worlds get extra alloys, set separately for free for all, fog and teams, so each start wins about as often when the computers play each other.
